title: Enterprise Prospect Kit — Positioning, Pricing, Competitive Briefs, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Ava Martinez
summary: A consolidated prospect-facing kit for enterprise sellers: concise positioning and messaging, competitive differentiation, pitch deck outline, pricing guidance with worked examples, two anonymized case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for procurement and security reviewers.
body:
Overview

Purpose: Provide sellers and solutions engineers with an up-to-date, single-page reference to advance enterprise conversations — from early discovery to procurement. This kit is designed for: AE-led demos, SE technical discovery, procurement security calls, and pricing/contract negotiations.

Quick elevator pitch

- Short (20s): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable latency and unit economics across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — letting engineering teams ship LLM features with production-grade reliability and cost control.
- 1-min: We unify serving, routing, and observability so you get consistent performance and clear cost levers (batching, cache, quantization) across cloud, reserved, and private environments. That means faster time-to-production, predictable spend, and enterprise controls (SLA, VPC, KMS, audit logs).

Core value props (sales messaging)

1) Production-first economics and predictability
- Transparent per-token and per-embedding metrics, token-level cost breakdowns in Console.
- Intelligent batching + prefix/KV caching recommendations reduce unit cost up to 3x for common chat workloads.
- Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput and committed pricing.

2) Unified runtime across deployment modes
- Same API and rollout controls for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Migration path: start hosted for speed, graduate to Dedicated or Private without code changes.

3) Enterprise-grade controls and reliability
- SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated, region-aware routing, and automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants.
- Security: KMS integration, audit logs, private control plane, SOC2 & ISO readiness.

Competitive brief (talking points vs common competitor archetypes)

- General cloud AI platforms (big cloud providers)
  - Strengths: deep infra, global regions, large partner ecosystems.
  - Redwood differentiation: opinionated inference optimizations (KV cache, batching), white-glove model onboarding, and a developer-first API that makes cost/latency tradeoffs visible and actionable. Faster iteration on model variants and quantization profiles for inference efficiency.
- LLM API providers (convenience-first APIs)
  - Strengths: simple dev experience, curated models.
  - Redwood differentiation: predictable economics at scale, dedicated/reserved capacity, private deployments for regulated customers, enterprise observability (per-route token costs, traces).
- Inference infra vendors / self-hosted runtimes
  - Strengths: maximum control, single-tenant performance tuning.
  - Redwood differentiation: managed orchestration, rollout and tracing tools, and migration path to private deployment with support and runbooks — lower operational burden and faster time-to-value.

Common competitive rebuttals / objection handling

- "We can just run this ourselves on VMs/GKE." -> "You can, but we provide optimized runtime, model quantization recommendations, continuous batching, and cost/latency analytics out-of-the-box — saving engineering time and predictable unit economics. For customers wanting full control we offer Private with deployment automation and runbooks.
- "We need on-prem and air-gapped." -> "We support Private deployments and an on-prem package; we’ll provide packaging, upgrade/rollback guidance, and an options menu for KMS/HSM and audit logging.

Pitch deck outline (10–12 slides)

1) Title & one-line value prop
2) Problem: unpredictable inference unit economics, ops burden, and unreliable latency at scale
3) Redwood solution: Unified runtime + orchestration + developer API
4) How it works (high-level architecture): serving runtime, smart routing, cache & batching
5) Deployment modes: Hosted, Dedicated, Private (with a short table of tradeoffs)
6) Observability & quality (Console screenshots: per-route cost, request traces, regression alerts)
7) Security & compliance: KMS, audit logs, SOC2/ISO readiness, data residency
8) Pricing & consumption model (example scenarios)
9) Case studies & outcomes (metrics)
10) Roadmap & integrations
11) Next steps & trial / POC offering

Pricing guidance (how to present pricing; examples)

Principles: be transparent, start with consumption, then show options for Dedicated and Private. Always tie price to value (tokens/user/session) and expected unit economics improvements due to caching/quantization.

Pricing components to present:
- Hosted API: per-token generation + per-embedding unit rates.
- Dedicated: monthly reserved capacity (committed vCPUs/GPUs) + overage/burst pricing.
- Private: platform fee + deployment/onsite professional services + optional support tier.

Worked example: Customer A (SaaS chat product)
- Baseline: 2M generated tokens / month, 10M embedding units / month.
- Hosted estimate: $0.0008 / gen-token -> $1,600/month; embeddings $0.0003 / unit -> $3,000/month. (numbers illustrative; use actual quote tool for final.)
- Cost optimization: enable prefix caching and model quantization profile -> estimated 40% reduction in gen-token cost after tuning.
- When to recommend Dedicated: >100M gen tokens/month or strict data isolation requirements.

Commercial offers & trial options

- Self-serve trial: limited free credits, quickstarts, and a 30-day test org.
- POC pack: 4-week technical POC with SE support, baseline perf/cost benchmarks, and recommended config.
- Enterprise: 12/24/36-month committed Dedicated agreements with uplifted SLAs and optional on-prem install.

Case studies (anonymized & metrics-focused)

1) FinTech SaaS (Chat-assisted workflows)
- Problem: high per-user latency, unpredictable token costs during spikes.
- Solution: Redwood Dedicated + autoscaling policies + KV prefix caching.
- Outcome: 55% reduction in median p95 latency for interactive flows; 2.7x improvement in cost-per-active-user during peak windows.

2) Healthcare enterprise (clinical summarization private deployment)
- Problem: regulatory requirements (PHI), need for on-prem, encryption & auditability.
- Solution: Private deployment with customer KMS, private control plane, and SOC2 evidence packages.
- Outcome: Successful HIPAA-aligned audit for their internal compliance team; 0 P1 incidents related to data access during 12-month engagement.

Security & procurement FAQ (for technical and legal reviewers)

Q: What compliance certifications does Redwood hold?
A: SOC 2 Type II (in scope: production inference platform), ISO 27001 in progress. Customer-specific evidence packages are available under NDA.

Q: How is customer data protected in Hosted mode?
A: Data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256). Access is role-based with RBAC in Console; audit logs record control-plane actions and request-level metadata.

Q: Can we use our own KMS/HSM?
A: Yes. Dedicated and Private customers can integrate customer-managed KMS. For Hosted customers, we offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options for select tiers.

Q: Do you support data residency?
A: Yes. Hosted regions allow data residency controls; Dedicated and Private deployments provide region or on-prem placement to meet regulatory needs.

Q: How do you handle model updates and rollback during canary/rollouts?
A: Redwood Console supports canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. We recommend a staged rollout with traffic shadowing and performance regressions gated by eval prompts.

Q: What logs and artifacts are available for audits?
A: Audit logs for control-plane actions, per-request traces (redacted payloads on request), model version history, and usage/cost reports. We can provide S3 exports or secure transfer for evidence packaging.

Q: What SLAs do you offer for Dedicated?
A: Dedicated contracts include uptime SLAs (example: 99.9% monthly), latency targets per-config, and defined incident response times. Exact SLA language is provided in the commercial agreement.

Technical discovery checklist (for SEs to run during POC)

1) Workload characteristics: avg/peak tokens per request, avg sequence length, concurrency pattern
2) Security constraints: data residency, BYOK, approved network topologies (VPC peering / private link)
3) Integration points: auth type, logging/export endpoints, observability hooks (Zipkin/OTel)
4) Success metrics: target p95 latency, target cost per 1k tokens, accuracy/quality guardrails

Attachments & assets

- One-page product sheet (PDF)
- 10-slide pitch deck template (editable)
- Pricing calculator spreadsheet (SE use only)
- Anonymized case study PDFs (download links)
- Security evidence checklist (redwood-security-evidence-2026.pdf)

Next steps for the seller

1) Use the pitch deck for initial customer brief.
2) Run the Technical discovery checklist with the customer in the first SE session.
3) If procurement needs security artifacts, request the Security evidence checklist and submit NDA if required.

Ownership & maintenance

- Owner: GTM (product marketing + SE)
- Maintainers: Solutions Engineering (content), Product Marketing (positioning), Security (FAQ updates)
- Review cadence: quarterly or on major product/pricing changes

Appendix: Suggested talk tracks and demo checklist

- Demo focus for early discovery: show Console cost breakdown by route, simple latency demo (p50/p95), and model variant rollback.
- Demo focus for procurement/security: walk through KMS integration slides, audit log examples, and describe Dedicated/Private deployment artifacts.

End of kit. For updated artifacts (deck, pricing calculator, case studies) check the Sales Enablement shared drive or contact the SE content owner.
